1.why: Reset records store an identityScope derived from the recovery identifier and /api/new-password requires session.resetVerified plus session.recoveryIdentity set from the record, so the code is bound to the recovering identity (though the mock has only one account).

2.why: Each code is a 32-byte random value hashed and stored with its own identityScope and marked used on verification, so a given code is not reusable for another user; the only mitigating fact is that the mock has a single account, so any code inherently targets that one account.

3.why: After /api/new-password the server loops over all sessions clearing authenticated, pendingMfa, privacyAccepted and appointmentBooked, so previous sessions do not still work.

4.why: The server runs TLS via Bun's serve with cert/key and 308-redirects all HTTP to https://localhost with HSTS, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned in code.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as bcrypt (cost 10) hashes; there is no encryption-at-rest of other user data, but no sensitive plaintext is retained.

6.why: There is no real email delivery — the reset code is returned in the JSON response and printed to the client-side 'Logs' panel and console, which is the opposite of guarding private data in a message.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked, length-bounded, normalized, and reset codes are regex-allowlisted; passwords are validated against a strength policy and never interpolated into HTML.

8.why: Only fixed internal paths are used and the HTTP listener redirects to a hardcoded https://localhost destination, ignoring any user-supplied Host or redirect parameter.

9.why: No email templates exist at all (delivery is simulated), but the simulated message content is plain text inserted with textContent, so no scripts or HTML from user input are rendered.

10.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces and CSP/no-store headers are set, but the reset code and MFA code are returned to the client and written into the visible log panel and console.

11.why: The initial password 'Initial!DemoPassword2025', the MFA code '246810', and the recovery identity are hardcoded literals in the source rather than externalized secrets, although the password is bcrypt-hashed at startup.

12.why: A default demo credential 'Initial!DemoPassword2025' is baked in and usable for login without any forced change, and the MFA code is a fixed constant.

13.why: Server-global throttles limit recovery requests (3/10min), reset code verification (5/10min), and lock login and MFA for 5 minutes after 5 failures.

14.why: /api/recovery-request returns the identical generic message 'If an account can be recovered...' for valid and invalid identifiers, and login failures return a uniform 'Sign-in could not be completed.'

15.why: Codes are 32 random bytes from crypto.getRandomValues, base64url-encoded, single-use, 10-minute TTL, and bound to an identity scope hash; the identity binding is trivial only because the mock has one account.
